    Irreducible ray arrows in the first radical layer #

    Concrete representatives of irreducible BGRS rays have nonzero classes in Jac(A) / Jac(A)^2. Distinct arrows incident to one vertex give linearly independent classes.

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.SplitBasicIdempotents.rayArrowRepresentative_not_mem_jacobson_sq {k : Type u} [Field k] {A : Type v} [Ring A] [Algebra k A] {ι : Type x} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (S : SplitBasicIdempotents) [Module.Finite k A] [HasBGRSDistributiveHomStructure k S.ProjectiveCategory] {x y : RayVertex S.RayCategory} (a : x ⟶ y) :
    ↑(Quotient.out ↑a) ∉ Ring.jacobson A * Ring.jacobson A

    A concrete representative of an irreducible BGRS ray has nonzero class in its primitive corner modulo Jac(A)^2.

    source
    theorem LargeIndecomposable.SplitBasicIdempotents.rayArrowLift_representative_not_mem_jacobson_sq {k : Type u} [Field k] {A : Type v} [Ring A] [Algebra k A] {ι : Type x} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (S : SplitBasicIdempotents) [Module.Finite k A] [HasBGRSDistributiveHomStructure k S.ProjectiveCategory] (L : BGRSRayArrowLift) {x y : RayVertex S.RayCategory} (a : x ⟶ y) :
    ↑(L.representative a) ∉ Ring.jacobson A * Ring.jacobson A

    Every representative selected by an arbitrary BGRS ray-arrow lift has a nonzero class in the ambient first radical layer.

    theorem LargeIndecomposable.SplitBasicIdempotents.outgoingRayRepresentatives_independent_mod_jacobson_sq {k : Type u} [Field k] {A : Type v} [Ring A] [Algebra k A] {ι : Type x} [Fintype ι] [DecidableEq ι] (S : SplitBasicIdempotents) [Module.Finite k A] [HasBGRSDistributiveHomStructure k S.ProjectiveCategory] {T : Type u_1} [Fintype T] {x : RayVertex S.RayCategory} (a : T → OutgoingQuiverArrow x) (ha : Function.Injective a) (c : T → k) (hsum : ∑ q : T, c q • ↑(Quotient.out ↑(a q).snd) ∈ Ring.jacobson A * Ring.jacobson A) (q : T) :
    c q = 0

    Distinct outgoing ray arrows determine linearly independent classes in the ambient first radical layer. This is stated without introducing a separate quotient-space API: a linear combination in Jac(A)^2 has all coefficients zero.

    The incoming version: distinct incoming ray arrows determine linearly independent classes in Jac(A)/Jac(A)^2.
